text: Company : Synchrony Bank Product : Credit card ( Venmo Visa ) Issue Type : Credit limit reduced/ over-limit status Desired Resolution : Correct reporting, explanation, and remediation Complaint Description I am submitting this complaint regarding my Venmo Visa credit card issued by Synchrony Bank. Synchrony reduced my credit limit without warning, which immediately caused my account to be reported as near or over the limit, despite no new purchases or charges being made. At the time of the credit limit reduction : My account was current I had not missed any payments I had not exceeded my prior credit limit The over-limit condition was caused solely by the issuers unilateral action This action created immediate financial and credit harm by : Artificially inflating utilization Creating an over-limit condition without consumer action Potentially damaging my credit profile due to issuer-initiated changes I contacted Synchrony to request : A temporary credit limit restoration, or Confirmation that the account would not be reported as over-limit due to an issuer-initiated limit reduction At this time, the matter remains unresolved. Why This Is a Problem While I understand issuers may reduce credit limits, doing so in a way that instantly penalizes the consumer without new spending is unfair and misleading, especially when the account is in good standing. This practice : Penalizes consumers for actions they did not take Creates avoidable credit reporting harm Lacks adequate notice or opportunity to respond I am requesting CFPB assistance to ensure this account is not reported as over-limit, and that any negative reporting resulting from the issuer-initiated credit limit reduction is corrected. Requested Resolution I respectfully request that Synchrony Bank : 1. Confirm the account will not be reported as over-limit due to an issuer-initiated credit limit reduction 2. Correct any negative reporting already submitted 3. Provide a written explanation for the credit limit reduction 4. title: Capital One — Credit card: Problem with a purchase shown on your statement
text: I have been a customer of Capital one for numerous of years. Capital One mailed out credit cards to my old address. I never received the cards that Capital One mailed. I reported to Capital one that I had moved and requested for them to change my address to my new current address. I contacted Capital One to dispute the fraudulent charges on the cards. Capital One was removing money from my bank account to cover charges on the credit card. I contacted Capital One to make them aware that they were taking money each month for the credit cards that I never received. I explained to Capital One that they had mailed new credit cards to my old address and someone at the old address was using the credit cards. But I had already informed Capital One of my new address. My Capital One credit cards were set up on automatic payment draft from my bank account ending in [REDACTED] ; I have never been late on a payment to Capital One. I dont understand how Capital One could continue to draft money from my bank account on credit cards I never received, nor have the cards. I have called Capital One numerous of times to try to resolve this problem. Capital One change the credit cards numbers and never sent me the new cards. I called Capital One to explain this to them. Capital One suspended my credit cards and trying to make me pay for credit cards that I havent never received or used. I received a bill from Capital One today in mail at my new address with a lot of interest charges as well as fraudulent charges. This is totally unfair to me, I have been a very good customer and never paid a bill late to Capital One. Capital one refuses to help me get my cards back.I had my Capital one cards set up online, Capital One deleted my account information, I have no online access to any of my card products from Capital One. This is illegal practice on Capital One behalf and I need help. I dont owe Capital One any money, they have been drafting money from my bank account for years to pay for fraudulent charges that they sent or said they sent to an old address of mine, I however called Capital One and made sure they had my current address. Sub-issue: Credit card company isn't resolving a dispute about a purchase on your statement. Sub-product: General-purpose credit card or charge card. Company response to consumer: Closed with non-monetary relief. Consumer state: AR. Date received by CFPB: 2021-06-26.

title: Goldman Sachs / Apple Card — Credit card: Trouble using your card
text: I am submitting this complaint regarding my Apple Card issued by Goldman Sachs and used for Apple purchases. I attempted to place an Apple order online using my Apple Card, but the transaction would not go through. Goldman Sachs later confirmed by phone that my card had been marked for fraud verification. The issue is that Apple checkout and Apple support did not clearly show or explain that this was the reason the purchase was blocked. Instead, I was left guessing what action I needed to take. Because the error handling and support guidance were unclear, I tried multiple steps myself to resolve the issue. This included paying off my Apple Card balance earlier than planned and then paying off my Apple Card installments as well. I took those actions because I believed, based on the unclear situation and support guidance, that the balance or installments might be preventing the Apple purchase from going through. However, the transaction still could not be completed with Apple Card. After that, I spent approximately [REDACTED] hours dealing with Apple and Goldman Sachs support through [REDACTED] chats and phone calls. I was repeatedly transferred between Apple and Goldman Sachs. Representatives gave inconsistent explanations or blamed the other side. There was no central case owner, no unified written thread, and no clear final resolution. I received multiple case numbers, including Apple case numbers [REDACTED] and [REDACTED], and Goldman Sachs case [REDACTED]. I was told there would be escalation or follow-up, but I did not receive a clear written explanation or resolution. Apple/Goldman later provided a complimentary [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] station worth approximately {$150.00}, which I appreciate, but that does not address the financial impact and time lost from the failed handling of this issue. My complaint is that Goldman Sachs/Apple Card fraud verification was not communicated properly through Apple checkout or support, which caused me to pay off my Apple Card balance and installments earlier than necessary, lose the ability to keep that cash in savings earning interest until the normal payment timeline, and spend approximately [REDACTED] hours trying to resolve the issue. Sub-issue: Can't use card to make purchases. Sub-product: General-purpose credit card or charge card. Company response to consumer: Closed with monetary relief. Consumer state: FL. text: [DATE]/[REDACTED] I opened a new Apple Card issued by Goldman Sachs. The new card offer includes a {$50.00} promotion. I tried to purchase Apple Music {$4.00} with my Apple Card to satisfy the requirement. However, the Apple payment system requires that I use my gift card balance in my account first ( I had over {$40.00} at that time ) and is not giving me the option to pay with my Apple Card. I contacted Goldman Sachs multiple times and emailed them 2 receipts ( Apple Music Purchase and an App purchase ) to prove that I did make the purchases but because of the Apple system setup there is no way I could pay for it with my Apple card issued by Goldman Sachs. They told me they will not give me the {$50.00} promotion because I did not use my card to purchase an Apple service. I explained many times over that I wanted to but the system wont let me. This is well documented on my account. I spoke with customer service representatives, 3 supervisors ( [REDACTED], [REDACTED], [REDACTED] [REDACTED] ) and finally a manager named [REDACTED] who did not want to give me his last name and who also told me there is NO ONE else he can escalate my issue to. [REDACTED] told me that I just have to use up all my gift card balance so I can then use the Apple Card to pay for an Apple service and therefore meet the requirement. I asked him why would I spend all my gift card balance, purchase Apple services I do not need only to get {$50.00}? So his solution is for me waste my $ [REDACTED]+ personal gift card balance on services I dont need to get the {$50.00} promotion. I also called Apple itself to see if they can help me since it is their payment system thats not giving me the option to pay with the Apple Card. I called [REDACTED] and the representative [REDACTED] opened a case # [REDACTED]. The purpose of the case is to have someone call me back from the Apple Promotional Team per a [REDACTED]. No one called me back. When I called back, I spoke with another rep and supervisor. Both confirmed that Apple requires that gift card balances should be used first before buyer can use a credit card payment. The supervisor told me that there is no promotional team who can help me and Apple cant help me and the only way is for me to spend all the money in the gift card balance ( {$43.00} as of [DATE]/[REDACTED] ) so I can then use my Apple Card and meet the {$50.00} promotion requirement. Please help me get the {$50.00} promotion I deserve. Sub-issue: Didn't receive advertised or promotional terms. Sub-product: Store credit card. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. text: Purchase Date : [DATE]/[REDACTED] Product : [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] : Apple Card Card Issuer : Goldman Sachs Problem : Apple Card Monthly Installment Plan For specific Apple products purchased with Apple Card. Amount : {$810.00} Installment amount : {$34.00} I purchased the [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] on [DATE]/[REDACTED] under the Apple Card Monthly Installment Plan for Apple products. The total amount, {$810.00} was applied in full to my Apple credit card. Not the monthly installment amount, {$34.00}. As a result, my available credit for purchase was reduced, an increased total remaining card balance, and Apple Card has reported information to the Credit Bureaus suggests a higher credit utilization rate with this card. During the phone call with the Apple Card Specialist, who helped me with the application and applying for the Monthly Installment Plan didnt fully disclose how the Monthly Installment Plan works or potential effects to credit and credit availability and overall interest charges that potentially will arise. Additionally, I have read and reviewed the availability information on the Apple Card website and the terms and conditions available in the Apple Card Customer Agreement pertaining to the Monthly Installment Plan. There is no mention, directly or indirectly of, the amount of the product being charged in full to the consumers credit card when purchased under the Monthly Installment Plan. Moreover, the consumer is forced to pay off their card balance in full before paying off the product purchased under the monthly installment plan. Apple Card & Goldman Sachs has drastically infringed on consumers abilities to manage personnel debts. For example the strategy of paying down/ off debts with the lowest interest rate. I am also concerned with interest charges. Apple states, customers wont pay interest on the specific item purchased on their card under the monthly installment plan. However, as I mentioned before, the total amount was applied to my card increasing my total card balance amount remaining/ owed. To my understanding interest charges are calculated using ones total card balance amount remaining/owed. I have reached out to Apple Card Services. I have talked with numerous Card Services Specialist and Supervisors on various occasions regarding my complaint. However, I have not heard from anyone else from Apple Card Services regarding my complaint. Moreover, in the documents and areas of information available to consumers previously mentioned it further creates confusion about the monthly Installment plan and is misleading when Apple/Goldman Sachs stated eligibility is subject to credit approval. Which suggests consumers will be subjected to another credit check to determine credit worthiness for the monthly installment plan separate from the current credit card account currently held. Lastly, the charges for the monthly Installment plan is always charged after the close of a billing cycle, creating a new charge for the next billing cycle even if I hadnt made no other purchases to produce a new bill Sub-issue: Confusing or misleading advertising about the credit card. title: Goldman Sachs / Apple Card — Credit card: Getting a credit card
text: Complaint Narrative For more than one year, I have been repeatedly and improperly denied an Apple Card due to a stated reason that is factually false and unsupported. Each denial states that an Apple Card or Apple Card application already exists for this user on another Apple Account and that Apple Card allows only one account per user. This is incorrect. I have never opened, held, or been approved for an Apple Card under any Apple ID, Social Security number, or identity. I have contacted Apple Card customer service numerous times. Apple Card representatives confirmed that : No Apple Card exists under my name No Apple Card exists under my Social Security number No Apple Card exists under any Apple ID associated with me My case was escalated multiple times to Apple Cards fraud department and internal back-office review. Each escalation confirmed that no account or prior application exists and that no fraud was identified. Despite these findings, the Apple Card system continues to automatically deny my applications for the same false reason. Apple and Goldman Sachs have failed and refused to correct the underlying system error or data misattribution. Customer service has stated they are unable or unwilling to fix it. As a result, I am indefinitely blocked from applying for credit based on incorrect internal information that the company itself can not identify or explain. This appears to be a failure of reasonable investigation, inaccurate internal recordkeeping, and an unfair credit denial based on non-existent information. Sub-issue: Application denied. Sub-product: General-purpose credit card or charge card. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: FL. Date received by CFPB: 2026-01-25.

text: I file this third complaint with the CFPB against Navient ( formerly [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] for the following reasons : In Navient 's response to the [REDACTED] prior CFPB complaints I filed last year, Navient indicated they would include a note to credit reporting agencies indicating I was disputing the debt Navient was reporting. In reviewing my credit report in [REDACTED] 2016, I find that Navient has failed to report to credit reporting agencies that I am disputing the debt Navient has refused to provide me with a breakdown of the payments I have made to them and what portion of those payments have been credited as interest, principal repayment, fees, and penalties Navient has refused to provide me with the formula they used to calculate the amount they claim is owed Navient continues to negotiate in bad faith. I have contested this debt, complained about Navient 's deceptive, unethical business practices, and have attempted to negotiate with Navient in good faith to reasonably settle the debt. Considering there can be no question that I have disputed this debt, Navient 's use of another debt collection agency is nothing more than another attempt at harassment and intimidation Prior CFPB complaint numbers : [REDACTED] [REDACTED] Sub-issue: Having problems with customer service. title: Navient — Student loan: Dealing with your lender or servicer
text: This is a complaint about both payment allocation and loan servicing customer service. After absentmindedly missing a payment I paid the full balance the following month, and, on a subsequent login to Navient 's website, the limited information available to me on Navient 's website showed that Navient had allocated the payment nearly equally between principal and interest ( allocation in prior month 's was about 70/30 principal/interest ). The information available to me on Navient 's website did not reflect allocation of payment to any fees. I submitted a request through Navient 's website for information regarding Navient 's calculation of the allocation. It took several days to get a response to this inquiry, and Navient 's answer was mere boilerplate - Navient 's answer referred me to the Promissory Note, without indicating specific sections or language, and without providing any analysis applying the terms of the Note to the allocation of payment to interest for my specific loan. Navient 's answer did not state that they had charged any fees. Meanwhile, Navient continues to charge interest. Although I submitted a new message through Navient 's online messaging platform, Navient 's messaging platform does not allow borrowers to " respond '' to communications from Navient, which unnecessarily interrupts the continuity of communications and tends to make it more difficult for borrowers to get answers from Navient and to restore their loans to fully paid-up status ( i.e. to make payments without fear of misallocation ). The lack of information about my loan on Navient 's website, Navient 's failure to provide information on request, Navient 's failure to respond timely to communications through their website, the fact that Navient does not provide a messaging platform that allows for cumulative correspondence in " threads, '' and the fact that Navient continues to charge interest during attempts to communicate about the loan all tend to suggest that Navient abusively inflates interest charges by delaying resolution of borrower questions to facilitate future payments. Sub-issue: Trouble with how payments are being handled. Sub-product: Private student loan. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: VA. Date received by CFPB: 2017-09-10.

title: Navient — Student loan: Dealing with your lender or servicer
text: I personally filed a complaint against Navient, alleging that Navient promised that my loan was eligible for public service loan forgiveness, only to find out later that my loans did not qualify. Phone recordings from Navient, selectively produced by Navient, seem to indicate that I was told my loans don't qualify. However, Navient never told me that my ineligible loans could be made eligible very easily by converting my loans to direct consolidated loans. I assumed that if my loans were not eligible for PSLF that I could never take advantage of PSLF. I didn't know that the nature of my loans could be changed, as Navient never told me they could. Instead, Navient told me I wasnt eligible for PSLF, but that there was good news because I qualified for lower payments with an income- based repayment plan. I have a phone recording from Navient ( given to me by Navient ), wherein a Navient supervisor tells me that Navient reps, once they know you are a public servant, are supposed to immediately notify you that to qualify for PSLF, you must convert to a direct loan. I posited that it must not be in Navient 's best interests to tell public servants about converting because that would mean that Navient loses my loan and interest payments to [REDACTED] [REDACTED]. The supervisor agreed with me. Then she reiterated that she was shocked that I wasn't told to convert to a direct loan. Navient has had my loan since [REDACTED]. Had they told me about converting to a direct loan back then, I would have been eligible for PSLF by [REDACTED]! Now, I'm not eligible until [REDACTED], 6 years after i'm scheduled to retire! I am also curious as to whether CFPB 's lawsuit against Navient is at least partially based on Navient, in order not to lose thousands of loans, not telling public servants of the need to convert to eligibility direct loans to qualify for PSLF. Sub-issue: Received bad information about your loan. Sub-product: Federal student loan servicing. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: IL. Date received by CFPB: 2019-02-26.

text: This is a follow-up to a complaint previously submitted to the CFPB. This complaint is being submitted simultaneously to the CFPB and to the [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] via [REDACTED]. Navient 's response to my complaint is misleading and ignores critical facts, as set forth below. I submitted to Navient the request to enroll my new bank account in AutoPay on [DATE]/[REDACTED] ( See Ex. D, attached ), confirmed by Navients [DATE]/[REDACTED] email to me. ( This email serves as confirmation of your request to enroll the loans below in Auto Pay. ) My old bank account had been enrolled continually in AutoPay for more than sixteen years up to that date. Navient had ample time between [DATE]/[REDACTED], when I submitted this information, and [DATE]/[REDACTED], to finalize [ ] the enrollment. Indeed, as Navients [REDACTED] email to me shows, this was Navients expectation, since that email explicitly stated that the Estimated Start Date for the new AutoPay arrangement was [REDACTED]the same day as the next payment due date. I reasonably relied on the representations in Navients [REDACTED] [REDACTED] email, and expected that the AutoPay payment would be made from the new account on [DATE]/[REDACTED]. Navient says that it was unable to extract my [REDACTED]. [REDACTED], [REDACTED] payment from my new bank, but gives no excuse why this was so, twenty days after Navient acknowledges I had furnished it with the information necessary for it take the payment. Any consequence of Navients unexcused delay in setting up AutoPaya delay Navient never bothered to report to memust fall upon Navient. Put another way, Navients statement that the account must be current is misleading. If the account was not current, it was because of Navients failure to timely set up AutoPay for the new bank when it had been given 20 days to do so. ( My mortgage servicer, to give one example, was able to activate my autopay capability with the same new bank within 24 hours of my request. ) At no time did Navient advise me that there was any difficulty in setting up the new AutoPay arrangements. Accordingly, the putative Administrative Forebearance was unlawfully imposed. I do not owe it, nor do I owe any expenses that flow from it. The arguments that Navient makes in its response about capitalizing interest, since they ignore Navients own responsibility for the delay in setting up AutoPay, are irrelevant. It also follows from these facts that my account was never past due, as Navient asserts. Even if these facts were not dispositive ( they are ), Navient also assured me through its customer service representative, on a recorded line, that my [DATE]/[REDACTED] payment would constitute timely payment for [REDACTED], and that my monthly payment going forward would be readjusted to the proper {$230.00}. Navients failure to honor this commitment would, on its own, constitute an unlawful unfair, deceptive, or abusive act under Sections 1031 and 1036 of the Dodd-Frank Act. I invite Navient to review the recording, and the law. Sub-issue: Trouble with how payments are being handled. Sub-product: Federal student loan servicing. title: Navient — Student loan: Getting a loan
text: My mother, an elderly ( [REDACTED] ) [REDACTED] [REDACTED], was taken advantage of by a former student, facilitated by the predatory lending practices of the lenders, initially to cosign on a [REDACTED] loan with encouragement from the lender and then she was duped into allowing the lender, Navient to make direct withdrawals from her bank account to make payments on the student loan. Navient directly withdrew the payments from my mothers account from [DATE]/[REDACTED] through the end of [REDACTED]. We discovered the withdrawals in [DATE]/[REDACTED] and immediately contacted Navient and insisted that they cease the withdrawals, yet they continued to make withdrawals for two more months. We then entered a stop payment order with my mothers bank yet Navient contested that stop payment order even knowing that they were not authorized to make such withdrawals. Navient engaged in predatory lending practices by directly facilitating the taking advantage of an [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] in order to receive payments on the [REDACTED] loan when it became apparent that the borrower was not willing or could not make payments. Navient admitted to us that it in fact talked with my mother in [DATE]/[REDACTED] at which time Navient laid out the options for her assuming responsibility for the loan payments. In doing so, Navient directly participated in taking advantage of my mothers compromised position. Navient knew that my mother had no familial relationship to the borrower. Instead of encouraging her to assume responsibility for the loan, Navient had the responsibility to explain the borrower 's right to loan forgiveness and to inquire further as to my mothers ability to make that decision to assume payments on the loan. My mother had no legal obligation to assume those loan payments, but Navient willingly accepted those payments despite her position as a [REDACTED] [REDACTED] who lacked the means to make those payments without adversely affecting her own financial condition. Navient failed to exercise due diligence in investigating my mothers capacity to make direct payments on behalf of the borrower. The result was that Navient participated in and facilitated the fraud against her. At the time Navient pressured my mother to assume responsibility for the loan, Navient had written documentation that my mother was living on a fixed income and lacked the means to make the payments without jeopardizing her own financial condition ( copy enclosed ). Navients actions were irresponsible and constituted predatory lending practices. We have reached out directly to Navient, but they refused to come even close to making my mother whole for losses from their wrongful withdrawals for more than 10 years from her account. They offered to return to her only about 20 % of what they took from her. We ask that Navient be ordered to repay my mother all monies that Navient withdrew from her account, with interest. Sub-issue: Fraudulent loan. Sub-product: Private student loan. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: VA. Date received by CFPB: 2021-02-05.

text: I am filing this complaint because Navy Federal Credit Union denied my fraud claim after I was targeted by someone impersonating Navy Federals Fraud Department. On [DATE]/year> at approximately [REDACTED][REDACTED] [REDACTED], I received an incoming call from someone I believed was Navy Federals Fraud Department. The call lasted approximately 53 minutes. During that call, the impersonator convinced me that there was fraud/security activity involving my account and instructed me to move money as part of what I believed was Navy Federals fraud protection process. Because I believed I was speaking with Navy Federal, I was fraudulently induced into moving funds connected to my checking account and [REDACTED] [REDACTED] The disputed transaction was {$2100.00}. Navy Federals own fraud update identified the transaction as suspected fraud involving [REDACTED] [REDACTED], posted on [DATE]/year>. Immediately after the impersonator call, I contacted the real Navy Federal number on [DATE]/year> at approximately [REDACTED] [REDACTED] That call lasted approximately 1 hour and 2 minutes. title: Bank of America — Checking or savings: Problem with a lender or other company charging your account
text: On [DATE]/23 ( according to my bank statement ), someone withdrew {$2000.00} then withdraw another {$1300.00} from my Bank of America Checking Account at a GAS STATION for a total of {$3300.00}. As soon as we realized the money was gone ( the same day ), my husband reported the fraudulent transaction ( THEFT ) to Bank of America. Bank of America claimed that they would conduct an investigation and advised us to remove the remaining money in the account so that the thief could not have access to it. In accordance with Bank of America 's instructions, my husband promptly went to a Bank of America ATM and withdrew {$1000.00} ( approximately what we had left in the account after the fraudulent transaction ). We waited for Bank of America to verify and refund the money. However, instead of refunding us the money from the fraudulent transaction that they allowed, Bank of America advised that they could not " find anything '' and so could not issue a refund. They did this instead of addressing our complaint that THEY, " Bank of America '' were GROSSLY NEGLIGENT for allowing a {$3300.00} -NON-CARD WITHDRWAL AT A GAS STATION and therefore should refund us the money. They told us that we should try to make the complaint with Bank of America to see if a second investigation would cause them to " find something '' warranting a refund. We subsequently submitted several complaints to Bank of America-all of which were terminated without Bank of America refunding us our money or taking any responsibility for their negligence. After a series of denied fraud complaints, I went to the Bank of America branch in [REDACTED] Florida and met the branch manager. she told also told me that Bank of America could not " find anything '' and also that there was no one from which to get the refund ( EVEN THOUGH THE MONEY WAS CLEARLY TAKEN AT A GAS STATION ) so Bank of America could not refund the money that Bank of America allowed someone to take from our account at a gas station. Lastly, it should be noted, that neither my husband nor I, have any history whatsoever of buying gas or spending in excess of {$100.00} at a gas station and so under no circumstance could it have been reasonable for Bank of America to believe that we were suddenly pumping {$3300.00} worth of gas.. Yet-Bank of America never contacted me nor my husband during or after the fraudulent transactions! It should also be noted that we never lost or misplaced our bank of America debit cards. It should be also noted that the transactions of {$2000.00} then {$1300.00} were two separate Non-card transactions and Bank of America authorized BOTH!. To date, Bank of America has failed to refund our money. We are two HARD WORKING people-just trying to make life. Perhaps to others, this may not be a big transaction, but for us-this loss caused by Bank of America , has caused devastating financial loss and problems. Sub-issue: Transaction was not authorized. title: Wells Fargo — Mortgage: Trouble during payment process
text: I am submitting a formal dispute of Wells Fargo Home Mortgages escrow accounting and refund determination related to my loan. On [DATE]/year>, Wells Fargo issued an Escrow Review Statement indicating an escrow overage of {$530.00}, which they refunded. However, this amount does not accurately reflect the excess escrow funds collected and retained in my account. Documented escrow over-collection : Wells Fargo collected escrow payments that exceeded actual escrow requirements for multiple consecutive months. From [REDACTED] through [DATE]/year>, escrow deposits exceeded projected needs by approximately {$100.00} per month, resulting in more than {$500.00} in excess collections, as shown in the escrow account history. Excess funds retained after major escrow obligations were satisfied : My largest escrow disbursements school taxes ( {$3600.00} paid [DATE]/year> ) and homeowners insurance ( {$1500.00} paid [DATE]/year> ) were completed early in the review period. Despite this, Wells Fargo continued to collect escrow and retained balances exceeding {$3500.00}, even though no significant near-term escrow obligations remained. Improper reliance on projection-based calculations : Wells Fargo calculated the refund amount using forward-looking projections rather than reconciling actual escrow needs at the time funds were held. This approach allowed Wells Fargo to retain excess funds for extended periods while issuing only a minimal refund, contrary to the intent of RESPA escrow requirements. Delayed and incomplete refund : The {$530.00} refund reflects Wells Fargos internally calculated minimum obligation, not the full amount of escrow funds improperly retained beyond lawful reserve needs. Pattern of escrow discrepancies : This issue is not isolated. It follows prior escrow discrepancies on this loan that required escalation, indicating a pattern of improper escrow administration rather than a one-time error. Sub-issue: Escrow, taxes, or insurance. Sub-product: Conventional home mortgage. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. text: I am writing to request correction of the error described below and to STOP the Trustees Sale scheduled for [DATE]/[REDACTED]. This is in regard to the mortgage on my property at [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED], CA [REDACTED]. Per the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, your company must respond to letter before the foreclosure sale. Because the trustee assumes the liability in auctioning the property in California a non-judicial foreclosure state, it would be in the trustees best interest not to foreclose on the property due to the following potential violations discovered before the Auction Sale Date. - The Trustee failed to issue a notice of default. The notice of default was done prior to ( you ) the trustee being assigned. This is a clear example of foreclosure laws and procedures. - Your company has violated the Consumer Finance Protection Bureau by Duel Tracking a foreclosure date after a complete loss mitigation application was received more than 37 days prior to a sale date. Your company denied my loan modification appeal on [DATE]/[REDACTED] ( see attached ). - Your company duel tracked a foreclosure date during this process of [DATE]/[REDACTED]. You are required to provide more than 37 days after such denial to the consumer before scheduling such foreclosure sale date. The CFPBs existing rules prohibit servicers from taking certain actions in foreclosure once they receive a complete loss mitigation application from a borrower more than 37 days prior to a scheduled sale. However, in some cases, borrowers are not receiving this protection, and servicers foreclosure counsel may not be taking adequate steps to delay foreclosure proceedings or sales. The CFPBs new rule clarifies that, if a servicer has already made the first foreclosure notice or filing and receives a timely complete application, servicers and their foreclosure counsel must not move for a foreclosure judgment or order of sale, or conduct a foreclosure sale, even if a third party conducts the sale proceedings, unless the borrowers loss mitigation application is properly denied, withdrawn, or the borrower fails to perform on a loss mitigation agreement. The clarifications will aid servicers in complying with, and assist courts in applying, the dual-tracking prohibitions in foreclosure proceedings to prevent wrongful foreclosures. - Your company has failed to acknowledge receipt of a NEW complete loss mitigation application received [DATE]/[REDACTED] on your website loanhelpstatus.bankofamerica.com and open a new loan modification process. -Your companys customer relationship manager [REDACTED] [REDACTED] on[DATE]/[REDACTED] said that none of the documents from [DATE]/[REDACTED] have been reviewed. text: I am filing a complaint regarding ongoing unauthorized debit card charges from [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] that have been occurring on my Chase checking account since [REDACTED]. I have never enrolled in [REDACTED] [REDACTED], never authorized these charges, and my [REDACTED] account confirms that no active [REDACTED] [REDACTED] subscription exists. Despite this, Chase allowed recurring charges to continue even after I disputed them. I contacted Chase by phone to report these charges as unauthorized recurring transactions and requested escalation to fraud. Chase failed to stop the charges, failed to provide a permanent merchant block, and refused to offer a meaningful resolution. Under Regulation E, Chase is required to properly investigate unauthorized debit card transactions, reimburse unauthorized charges, and prevent further unauthorized withdrawals. Chase did not meet these obligations. I have provided documentation showing that no [REDACTED] [REDACTED] membership exists and that the charges were not authorized. The continued approval of these charges represents a failure in Chases fraud prevention and dispute handling processes. This situation has caused financial loss, repeated disputes, and significant time spent attempting to resolve an issue Chase is legally required to handle. When I contacted Chase by phone, I was told that they could not assist because the charges were outside a 30-day limit. This response is inadequate and misleading. While Chase may impose internal dispute deadlines, Regulation E requires banks to address unauthorized recurring transactions and prevent future unauthorized withdrawals once notified. Chase failed to stop the recurring charges after notification and failed to escalate the issue to fraud, effectively allowing continued unauthorized withdrawals from my account. Sub-issue: Transaction was not authorized. Sub-product: Checking account. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: MI. Date received by CFPB: 2026-01-25.

text: am filing a complaint regarding overdraft fees assessed on my Chase Total Checking account. I am paid weekly, with regular direct deposits of approximately {$850.00} or more every Friday, yet my account is unable to recover due to Chases overdraft practices. I was charged for overdraft protection even though no overdraft protection was provided. This created a recurring cycle where : My account went slightly negative, Overdraft fees posted immediately, Retried ACH and recurring transactions posted, Additional overdraft fees were assessed, Incoming deposits were consumed by prior fees before stabilizing the account. I have contacted Chase customer service and spoken with three supervisors, clearly explaining that I am being charged overdraft fees without transactions being paid. Despite providing this information, Chase has refused to resolve the issue and offered only {$100.00} in refunds, which does not address the scope or systemic nature of the problem. I am not disputing that some transactions were presented when funds were low. I am disputing being charged overdraft fees without the bank actually covering the transactions, resulting in fees being assessed for a service that was not rendered. I am requesting : 1. Reimbursement of overdraft fees charged during this period, and 2. Review of Chases overdraft fee practices when transactions are not paid but fees are still assessed. title: Synchrony — Debt collection: Written notification about debt
text: The attached collection never proved any right to collect a debt, which requires according to the Federal Trade Commission, Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and my rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act not only a statement that the collection agency or debt buyer is trying to collect on a debt. but there must also be given to the consumer a sign off statement from the original showing documentation that the debt collector was assigned permission to collect a particular debt, but since the US Supreme Court decision on [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED], there are hundreds of collection agencies now identifying themselves as debt buyers. This decision basically throws out my rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act completely. There is a big problem with collection agencies now classifying themselves as debt buyers. The first problem is that almost all states are now requiring separate licensing for such a designation. Most debt collection agencies are avoiding that requirement nationwide. In addition, there must be a written statement from the original debtor showing proof of new ownership. A simple letters from a debt collector will not stand up in any state court. The attached collection/debt ownership is invalid based upon the fact that in most cases a collection agency can not show proof of assignment or new debt ownership. Almost all credit card ownership has been sold to securitized pooling agreements. This is factual which means one thing, how can the original procurer of a debt assign collections or new debt ownership without approval from the original securitized trust without buying the debt back itself. The simple math proves otherwise. This letter of the right to collect either on collection assigned rights or new debt ownership is invalid based upon the disconnect of rights. Accordingly, the collection is invalid and can not have validity unless its given back to the original debt procurer. I am not disputing the obligation of debt. The collection agencies have already abused the [REDACTED] decision causing billions in financial damages to the American consumer. This collection is in essence invalid and my file should be purged and any reference to a collection on my credit bureaus must be deleted permanently. Sub-issue: Didn't receive enough information to verify debt. Sub-product: Credit card debt. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Official interpretation of 13 ( b ) Billing Error Notice 1. Withdrawal of billing error notice by consumer. The creditor need not comply with the requirements of 1026.13 ( c ) through ( g ) of this section if the consumer concludes that no billing error occurred and voluntarily withdraws the billing error notice. The consumer 's withdrawal of a billing error notice may be oral, electronic or written. 2. Form of written notice. The creditor may require that the written notice not be made on the payment medium or other material accompanying the periodic statement if the creditor so stipulates in the billing rights statement required by 1026.6 ( a ) ( 5 ) or ( b ) ( 5 ) ( iii ), and 1026.9 ( a ). In addition, if the creditor stipulates in the billing rights statement that it accepts billing error notices submitted electronically, and states the means by which a consumer may electronically submit a billing error notice, a notice sent in such manner will be deemed to satisfy the written notice requirement for purposes of 1026.13 ( b ). title: Affirm — Credit reporting: Incorrect information on your report
text: I am submitting a complaint regarding several Buy Now, Pay Later ( BNPL ) purchases through Affirm, which are incorrectly reported to [REDACTED] as unsecured personal loans. These transactions were short-term installment plans, each with a repayment period of 3 or 6 months, not traditional credit products. Here are the Affirm accounts in question as they appear in my [REDACTED] report : [REDACTED]. Account : [REDACTED] Opened [DATE]/[REDACTED][REDACTED] {$510.00} Paid off by [DATE]/[REDACTED][REDACTED] Reported as Unsecured loan 2. Account : [REDACTED] Opened [REDACTED] [REDACTED], [REDACTED] {$630.00} Term : 3 months Still open Reported as Unsecured loan 3. Account : [REDACTED] Opened [REDACTED] [REDACTED], [REDACTED] {$210.00} Term : 6 months Still open Reported as Unsecured loan 4. Account : [REDACTED] Opened [REDACTED] [REDACTED], [REDACTED] {$200.00} Term : 3 months Still open Reported as Unsecured loan 5. Account : [REDACTED] Opened [REDACTED] [REDACTED], [REDACTED] {$180.00} Term : 3 months Still open Reported as Unsecured loan These are BNPL purchases, not traditional loans. Affirms own reporting labels them as Buy Now Pay Later, and they were all paid or are being paid on time. However, reporting them as unsecured personal loans has negatively impacted my credit score. I contacted both Affirm and [REDACTED] requesting correction, but both denied any wrongdoing. Im attaching screenshots from Affirm and my [REDACTED] report for proof. I request that these be correctly reclassified as short-term BNPL accounts or removed if they are not credit-impacting according to Affirms BNPL policy. Sub-issue: Account information incorrect. Sub-product: Credit reporting. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: WA. Date received by CFPB: 2025-05-27.

issue: Credit monitoring or identity theft protection services
title: Affirm — Credit reporting: Credit monitoring or identity theft protection services
text: I am submitting this complaint regarding an unauthorized loan issued by Affirm for a [REDACTED] [REDACTED] purchase under my name. I never applied for or approved any purchase from [REDACTED] [REDACTED] nor did I apply for a Buy Now, Pay Later ( BNPL ) loan through Affirm. Upon contacting Affirm, I was provided the following details : [REDACTED] [REDACTED] Order ID : [REDACTED] Affirm Loan ID : [REDACTED] Loan Amount : {$1200.00} Affirm informed me that this loan was issued using my personal information, including my name, date of birth, and residential address. However, the phone number on file with Affirm did not match mine. I made it clear that I did not authorize this loan or transaction. I requested Affirm to immediately investigate and freeze this loan. Affirm opened a dispute under Case # [REDACTED] on [DATE]/year>, and I was advised the investigation could take up to 30 days. During this process, I discovered that the Affirm loan had been reported on my [REDACTED] credit report. I immediately filed a dispute with Affirm, and the record was successfully removed from my [REDACTED] report on [DATE]/year>. I am filing this complaint with your agency because my personal information and identity may have been used without my knowledge in other instances as well, potentially impacting my credit reports at other credit bureaus. I respectfully request that your office investigate this matter further and advise me on any additional steps I should take to protect myself from further unauthorized use of my personal and financial information. Thank you for your attention and assistance. Sub-issue: Billing dispute for services. Sub-product: Credit reporting. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: TX. Date received by CFPB: 2025-08-30.

title: JPMorgan Chase — Credit card: Incorrect information on your report
text: I have an account with Chase bank for a Southwest Airlines Credit Card. The original limit was {$12000.00}. There is an annual fee of {$90.00}. Shortly after charging and collecting the annual fee, Chase reduced my credit limit from {$12000.00} to {$3300.00}. This reduction was executed [DATE]/[REDACTED] of 2020. I had just paid down the balance from {$12000.00} to {$3300.00} from [REDACTED] through [REDACTED]. The reduction in credit limit put me over my credit limit. I called Chase around [DATE]/2020 and they said they ran their random account review and that resulted in a lower credit limit. I asked why the limit was set below the remaining balance as this would put me over my limit and be consider negative on my credit report. They said it would not show on my credit report as they have not reported it to the bureaus yet. I started receiving credit monitoring notifications from multiple sources ( [REDACTED], [REDACTED], Chase ) that I had new negative account activity to include a large reduction in available credit ( lost $ [REDACTED] in available credit ) and a card reporting over the limit ( this Chase account at {$3300.00}, or {$9.00} over the limit ). I don't believe companies should be eligible for charging renewals and then drastically cutting credit limits. They should conduct the review and if there is a change in terms then its the consumers option to continue the account relationship at the expense of the annual fee. That is not fair I paid {$90.00} to have my limit cut by over 70 %. Additionally, I was not provided enough time to react to their insane credit reduction to prevent myself from being reported over the limit. [REDACTED] weeks is not enough time for them to send me the communication and allow me to take action to reduce the balance before reporting me over the limit. I want any reference to being over the credit limit removed from all bureau reports. Sub-issue: Account information incorrect. Sub-product: General-purpose credit card or charge card. title: JPMorgan Chase — Credit card: Problem with a purchase shown on your statement
text: I agreed to purchase some goods from a vendor in a certain timeframe, which was guaranteed at the time of purchase. When the goods did not arrive, I emailed the vendor in advance of the deadline reminding them of our agreement. The goods still did not arrive by the deadline we had agreed at the time of pirchase. The Fair Credit Billing Act, 15 U.S. Code 1666, ( b ) ( 3 ) defines a billing error as " A reflection on a statement of goods or services ... not delivered to the obligor or his designee in accordance with the agreement made at the time of a transaction. '' I complained to my credit card company about this billing error and forwarded copies of the emails which demonstrated the agreement made at the time of the transaction and how it was breached. I pointed out to the card company that the vendor had accepted responsibility for the billing error and wrongly offered me a 50 % refund of my money- which I refused. However, Chase Card Services refused to accept that this was a billing error and wrote to me to say " We found no evidence of a billing error based on our research. '' This conclusion was reached even though the vendor had admitted the billing error This is the second time is as many months that Chase has refused to accept an obvious billing error as a billing error. After I complained to you on the previous occasion, Chase immediately reversed its initial decision and accepted the previous complaint as a billing error. They will do the same here. The basis of this complaint is that Chase is SYSTEMATICALLY avoiding legitimate billing errors. Sub-issue: Credit card company isn't resolving a dispute about a purchase on your statement. Sub-product: General-purpose credit card or charge card. Company response to consumer: Closed with monetary relief. Consumer state: NY. Date received by CFPB: 2021-11-10.

title: JPMorgan Chase — Credit card: Other features, terms, or problems
text: Chase credit card automatically allows credit card spending to go over the credit limit. I did not sign up for this feature or did I have the ability to utilize the website or all to remove this option. Once I went over the credit limit my account was frozen because I was forced to pay off the debt to unfreeze the account. Essentially this is a marketing deception of zero APR credit cards to allow a credit limit but not allow credit limit protections so when the amount is breached that the credit card declines any purchases that go over the credit limit. Thus when I breached the credit limit that the payment was allowed but it shouldnt have allowed this thus my account was frozen and I was forced to pay debt to unfreeze the account as a conflict of zero APR period credit cards being a fraudulent marketing deception when credit limit protections do not exist on the initial purchases but deceived those that believe that the credit limit is a true limit and that another over the limit should be declined thus a marketing scam when I am forced to pay on zero APR to unfreeze the account when I could have an unfrozen account without needing to pay down any debt immediately as a credit card scam. I was told you can only call in to remove this option and that I could not do so while the account was frozen as they could not unfreeze until the debt was covered above the limit. This essentially creates a cover charge as a hidden fee to zero APR credit cards and should be illegal as a concern for hidden fees and obligation to pay debt down immediately. Sub-issue: Other problem. Sub-product: General-purpose credit card or charge card. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: IL. Date received by CFPB: 2023-10-01.

title: Wells Fargo — Money transfer: Other transaction problem
text: I needed to transfer money from [REDACTED] [REDACTED], [REDACTED] MS to Wells Fargo. I had to add [REDACTED] [REDACTED] to my Wells Fargo account as an authorized bank. I followed all of Wells Fargo bank-to-bank transfer validation procedures to add [REDACTED] [REDACTED]. I received notification that [REDACTED] [REDACTED] was added to Wells Fargo. Wells Fargo stated the maximum amount that could be transferred was {$5000.00}. I made the transfer transaction through Wells Fargo and received an email on [DATE]/19 from Wells Fargo stating that my transfer was being processed ( see attached email ). The next day, [DATE]/19, I received an email ( see attached ) from Wells Fargo Security Fraud that unusual activity was seen in my Wells Fargo account and my account was locked. I contacted Wells Fargo Security Fraud and they stated even though I followed the correct procedures to transfer money, that is how fraud starts. They directed me to go into a Wells Fargo branch and show them my [REDACTED] [REDACTED] statement and identification to prove that the [REDACTED] [REDACTED] was truly my account. I did what Wells Fargo wanted me to do and my account was unlocked. On [DATE]/19, it became apparent to me that my {$5000.00} transfer had never been applied to my Wells Fargo account. I have called Wells Fargo everyday this week, spoke to numerous Wells Fargo employees about my missing money. They created an investigative case number [REDACTED]. A [REDACTED] [REDACTED] employee made a 3-way call with me to Wells Fargo to attempt to resolve the missing money. Wells Fargo has stated when Wells Fargo Security Fraud froze my account that the transfer transaction was cancelled and the money was returned to [REDACTED] [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] [REDACTED] was able to contact Wells Fargo ACH department and obtained a trace number for the credit from [REDACTED] [REDACTED] associated with a debit to Wells Fargo. Wells Fargo ACH department was unable to locate a trace number for a credit going back to [REDACTED] [REDACTED]. The [REDACTED] [REDACTED] employee tried to explain to the investigative case workers at Wells Fargo that since an off-setting credit trace number was not available in their ACH files, the money was probably in their unposted funds account. Wells Fargo is very adamant that the money was sent back to [REDACTED] [REDACTED] but could not provide any trace numbers to prove that fact. [REDACTED] [REDACTED] has searched their ACH files to ensure nothing was missed on their end. My money has not been in either account for over a month and is nowhere to be found. During my final conversation on [DATE]/19 with Wells Fargo executive investigative department, I informed them I would be filing a complaint with the CFPB and they said " OK ''. It appears to me they do not care about my missing {$5000.00}. I firmly believe when the Wells Fargo Security Fraud department froze my account, the money was cancelled from being put into my Wells Fargo account and it was not transferred back to [REDACTED] [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] [REDACTED] agrees with my belief that my money is somewhere within the Wells Fargo financial institution. Sub-product: Domestic (US) money transfer. text: Unauthorized Gym Membership Charge Bank Wrongly Denied Dispute Summary : I am reporting repeated unauthorized charges by [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED][REDACTED] on my Wells Fargo credit card account. The gym has charged me without my authorization, engaged in deceptive practices to keep me enrolled in their program, and refused to provide refunds. The contract they rely on does not bear my signature, so I never formally agreed to these charges. The gym has also threatened to ban me from the facility when I questioned or disputed these charges. Despite disputing the charges with my bank, the bank denied my disputes, leaving me without recourse. Details of Unauthorized Charges : - [DATE]/[REDACTED] {$830.00} : Unauthorized charge. I was unable to dispute this charge with my bank at the time because it was past 90 days, but I never authorized it. - [DATE]/[REDACTED] {$850.00} : Unauthorized charge. I filed a dispute with my bank ; the dispute was denied. - [DATE]/[REDACTED] {$850.00} : Unauthorized charge. I filed a dispute with my bank ; the dispute was denied. - [DATE]/[REDACTED] {$1600.00} : Unauthorized charge. I filed a dispute with my bank ; the dispute is currently pending. Supporting Facts : The gyms behavior appears to be a pattern of misleading and coercive practices, including : - I never signed any contract with this gym there is no signed authorization from me for recurring billing. - The gym has engaged in deceptive and coercive practices, pressuring me to remain in the program while refusing refunds for unauthorized charges. - The gym refused to cancel the recurring charges upon request. - The gym refused to refund for unauthorized charges. - The gym continued to make unauthorized charges despite complaints. - The gym threatened to ban me from the facility when I questioned or disputed charges. - The bank denied my disputes for the charges on [DATE]/[REDACTED] and [DATE]/[REDACTED] despite clear evidence that they were unauthorized. These repeated unauthorized charges have caused financial harm, stress, and inconvenience, and may continue if the gyms practices are not investigated. What I am requesting : - That the bank reopen and properly investigate all disputes, including the charge on [DATE]/[REDACTED], which I could not dispute initially. - That the bank require the merchant to provide actual proof of authorization, rather than generic or boilerplate documents. - That all unauthorized charges be refunded promptly. - That the bank ensure its investigation and resolution comply with : + Regulation E ( EFTA ) for unauthorized transactions + [REDACTED] chargeback rules for recurring billing + Fair Credit Billing Act Additional Notes : I request that the CFPB consider all four charges as part of a pattern of ongoing unauthorized billing. This demonstrates the gyms repeated malpractice and disregard for consumer consent. I urge the CFPB to take prompt action to prevent further unauthorized charges and to protect other consumers from similar practices. I believe Citi Student Loan has sold the loans off and did not receive the payment I have records for and continue to collect and hold me liable. I am yet to hear directly from Citi Student Loans on the proof of payments I have submitted to them and a reconciliation of the loans I paid off. They can not show any proof with the payment I made and how they were applied to the loan and why they continue to show a balance on the Student Loan accounts and reporting the account as charge off collection. These inaccurate reporting by Citi Student Loan has damaged my credit rating and caused me to be turned down by banks, and financial agencies. I am exhausted at dealing with Citi Student Loan and have no other place to turn to get them to correct and fix this error. I only ask that they reconcile the account and show me how my payments I've made of the years were applied to the loans I borrowed and explain why I owe them a balance they are claiming when my records showed I paid the loans off. Since I've contacted Citi Student Loan and can not get them to provide me this information it seems that they are taking part in collection practice that is illegal and violation of the fair credit reporting act. If I could afford to file a lawsuit against Citi Student Loan I would have done so as their response to my letters and their lack of providing proof of the debt and payment I made to Citi Student Loan and its Creditors is something they have yet to provide me. sub_issue: Lender trying to repossess or disable the vehicle
title: Capital One — Auto loan: Repossession
text: My vehicle was repossessed by a company hired by Capital One Auto Finance. The repossession occurred on Friday, [DATE]/[REDACTED] at approximately [REDACTED] [REDACTED] and involved illegal entry into a secured, restricted-access residential garage at my apartment building, The [REDACTED] in [REDACTED], Connecticut. The garage is private and requires a resident parking pass/fob for entry. It is not open to the public. Building management reviewed security footage and confirmed in writing that the repossession agent entered the garage without authorization by improperly accessing the garage through the exit. No permission was granted by building management for the repossession company to enter the garage, and the incident was captured on video, which I have retained. Under Connecticut [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED], a repossession may only occur if it can be completed without breach of the peace. Unauthorized entry into a secured residential garage constitutes a breach of the peace and renders the repossession improper and unlawful. Although the repossession has already been reported on my credit, I am formally disputing the accuracy of that reporting because it is based on an improper repossession that involved unlawful entry into private, secured property. I am requesting CFPB assistance to ensure that Capital One Auto Finance : Conducts a full investigation into the unlawful conduct of its contracted repossession agent Waives all repossession-related, towing, and storage fees Places the account on hold while the investigation is pending Provides a reinstatement option without penalty Corrects or removes any negative credit reporting related to this improper repossession Video evidence and written confirmation from building management are available and can be provided upon request. Sub-issue: Lender trying to repossess or disable the vehicle. Sub-product: Lease. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: CT. Date received by CFPB: 2026-01-16.

I was told to text a list of numbers to a text message in an attempt to retrieve the money stolen. Unknowingly I sent payments to an unauthorized person through zelle. The person on the phone gave me their call back number and name. I called back the number and it was not a chase representative. I received an email from chase stating that these payments looked suspicious and they were going to be investigated. I went to the bank to get the issue resolved in person. My account was closed to eliminate any further scam charges. I was told by the bank associate I had to wait for a letter in the mail explaining the situation so I can take it to the precinct. Weeks later I called the fraud department at chase and was told they dont produce letters that can be used to show proof of a scam. They are also refusing to investigate the payments sent through zelle or refund me the money. Sub-product: Mobile or digital wallet. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: NJ. Date received by CFPB: 2025-10-27.

title: Capital One — Checking or savings: Managing an account
text: I am filing this complaint to draw the CFPBs attention to the unfair and deceptive practices of Capital One in connection with its Capital One 360 Savings Accounts and request that I be made whole for the lost interest that I would have earned had Capital One not engaged in these practices. I have held multiple high-interest savings accounts with Capital One for more than a decade. All were opened as high-interest savings accounts under [REDACTED] [REDACTED] and transferred to Capital One 360 Savings Accounts when Capital One acquired [REDACTED] [REDACTED]. Interest rates on those accounts adjusted as interest rates declined after the acquisition. In [REDACTED], Capital One created a new variable rate savings account product with a similar name, Capital One 360 Performance Savings Account, and no longer offered Capital One 360 Savings Accounts to new customers. Capital One 360 Performance Savings Accounts were the only variable savings accounts advertised by Capital One starting in [REDACTED]. As interest rates rose over the past few years, the interest rates on Capital One 360 Savings Accounts were not adjusted. In contrast, Capital One 360 Performance Savings Accounts were adjusted and widely advertised as having competitive rates. Because of the similar name and the fact that the Capital One 360 Performance Savings Accounts were the only variable savings accounts on the banks website, Capital One deceived me and other longstanding depositors with Capital One 360 Savings Accounts who reasonably thought that they were benefiting from the high-yield variable rates advertised by Capital One. Capital One also was unfair to its longstanding depositors because the material difference in the interest rate offered on existing savings accounts was not adequately communicated to existing savings account holders. As recently as [DATE]/[REDACTED], I contacted Capital One customer service to consolidate some of my Capital One 360 Savings Accounts. I now know that, at the time, my Capital One 360 Savings Account was paying only 0.30 % interest while the Capital One 360 Performance Savings Accounts were paying 4.3 % interest. I was not informed that the rate on Capital One 360 Savings Accounts was no longer being adjusted, that the accounts were not being offered anymore to customers, or that there was a similar savings account with a much higher interest rate that any reasonable person would have converted their account to. I was made aware of this issue yesterday from a newspaper article about a potential class action lawsuit. I called Capital One, transferred my money to Capital One 360 Performance Savings Accounts, and filed a complaint. The unfair and deceptive practices of Capital One have cost me and others substantial interest over an extended period of time. Furthermore, these practices are ongoing for those who still do not realize that Capital One pulled a bait and switch on their savings accounts. I request that I be made whole by adjusting the interest rate on my Capital One 36 0 Savings Account retroactively to be what was advertised for Capital Ones variable rate savings account ( i.e., to be paid the interest that I would have earned had my account been converted to a Capital One 360 Performance Savings Account when Capital One 360 Savings Accounts were no longer advertised to new customers ). Sub-issue: Banking errors. Sub-product: Savings account. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: DC. Date received by CFPB: 2023-11-10.

title: JPMorgan Chase — Auto loan: Managing the loan or lease
text: I filed a [REDACTED] [REDACTED] bankruptcy over a year ago. Bankruptcy Case Number : [REDACTED]. I submitted a Statement of Intention ( [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] ) explicitly indicating that my vehicle loan was not included in the bankruptcy estate. JPMorgan Chase received this filing and has acknowledged that the vehicle was not part of the bankruptcy. A bankruptcy court hearing occurred, and Chase did not appear or object, as reflected in the court record of appearances. Despite this, Chase continues to internally code the vehicle loan and VIN as bankruptcy-related. A Chase bankruptcy representative [REDACTED] acknowledged that the vehicle was not included in the bankruptcy and that I completed the required form, yet Chase has refused to remove the bankruptcy designation. Because of this incorrect classification, other banks and credit unions are unable to refinance the vehicle, as the VIN returns as bankruptcy-coded when lenders attempt to process refinancing. Chase representatives initially stated the loan could potentially be refinanced internally as a used car loan, which would remove the bankruptcy designation. However, Chase later refused to refinance the vehicle or correct the bankruptcy coding, leaving the loan incorrectly flagged. The vehicles VIN is [REDACTED]. Chase is associating this VIN with Bankruptcy Case Number [REDACTED], even though the vehicle was never listed, scheduled, discharged, or reaffirmed in the bankruptcy. This inaccurate servicing designation is preventing refinancing, interfering with normal loan servicing, and contradicting the bankruptcy court process. I am requesting that JPMorgan Chase remove all bankruptcy designations associated with this vehicle and VIN, correct all internal and third-party reporting, and confirm in writing that the loan is not bankruptcy-involved, so refinancing may proceed. Sub-issue: Billing problem. Sub-product: Loan. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: OR. Date received by CFPB: 2025-12-09.

title: Goldman Sachs / Apple Card — Checking or savings: Managing an account
text: On [DATE]/year>, I was the victim of fraud involving my Apple ID, Apple Card, Apple Savings Account, and Apple [REDACTED] A scammer gained control of my Apple ID and changed the trusted phone number, locking me out of the account. At the time, I had an Apple Credit Card and an Apple Savings Account with approximately {$2600.00} in rewards funds. Those funds were transferredwithout my authorizationfrom Apple Savings to Apple [REDACTED] ( which is operated by [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED]. The scammer then used the Apple [REDACTED] funds at [REDACTED] to purchase multiple gift cards. I immediately reported the fraud to Apple, Goldman Sachs ( issuer of Apple Card and Apple Savings ), and [REDACTED] [REDACTED] ( operator of Apple [REDACTED] ). However : Apple has been unwilling to help me recover access to my account or funds. Goldman Sachs has only disputed charges on the credit card, not the stolen savings. [REDACTED] [REDACTED] is disputing the gift card purchases with [REDACTED], but has stated that any recovered funds will be returned to the Apple [REDACTED] account associated with the hackers Apple IDwhich I can not access. This leaves me in an impossible position : my legitimate funds have been stolen, and the companies involved are refusing to restore them to me. If [REDACTED] issues a refund, those funds will not be returned to me, the rightful account holder, but to the fraudsters account. I believe these institutions are failing in their duty to protect consumers. Apple, Goldman Sachs, and [REDACTED] [REDACTED] should not allow a hacked Apple ID to permanently deprive me of funds held in federally regulated financial products. Resolution I am seeking : Restoration of my {$2600.00} to me, the rightful owner. Assurance that any disputed/refunded funds from [REDACTED] will not be deposited back into the compromised Apple [REDACTED] account but instead credited to me directly. Improved consumer protections to prevent this situation from happening to others. Sub-issue: Problem accessing account. Sub-product: Savings account. title: Affirm — Payday / personal loan: Struggling to pay your loan
text: 1. Unfair and Inaccurate Negative Credit Reporting : I am writing to file a formal complaint against Affirm for unfair and inaccurate credit reporting practices. Specifically, Affirm has reported late payments on my credit report, negatively impacting my credit score. However, Affirm has never reported any of my previous on-time payments to the credit bureaus. This selective reporting, where only negative information is shared, is fundamentally unfair and misleading. This practice creates a skewed perception of my creditworthiness, as it only reflects negative events without any corresponding positive payment history. 2. Lack of Consistent Reporting Standards : It is my understanding that Buy Now, Pay Later ( BNPL ) companies, including Affirm, should not report negative information if they have not consistently reported positive payment history. This is based on the principle that a complete and accurate credit profile requires a balanced representation of both positive and negative financial behavior. Many consumer advocacy groups and financial experts have raised concerns about the inconsistent reporting practices of BNPL companies. Reporting only negative data creates an incomplete and potentially damaging picture of a consumer 's creditworthiness. It is my understanding that the CFPB has been looking into the BNPL sector, and the unfair practices that are being used. [REDACTED]. Difficulty Accessing Assistance During Financial Hardship : Furthermore, Affirm does not provide easily accessible avenues for customers to seek assistance during periods of financial hardship. Navigating their customer service channels to request payment arrangements or other forms of support is unnecessarily difficult and frustrating. This lack of transparency and accessibility exacerbates the negative impact of late payments, particularly during unforeseen financial challenges. I have attempted to contact them and have received no assistance. Sub-product: Installment loan. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Consumer state: MI. Date received by CFPB: 2025-02-25.

title: Citibank — Payday / personal loan: Problem when making payments
text: Something that has happened to me makes me realize what can go wrong with Buy Now, Pay Later ( BNPL ) credit products : I am getting billed {$1800.00} for a fridge I do not have and there is no central point of responsibility in these BNPL schemes to fix the problem. I purchased a fridge from [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] on a BNPL scheme. I even bought the extended warranty. The fridge came with a broken cooling mechanism and could not get below 75 degrees. So, I invoked the warranty and found out I was really dealing with Summit Appliance because that is who made the model of the fridge I purchased. So far, so good. The fridge could not be repaired and so [REDACTED] said they would process my claim for a full refund. I have that in writing. I never heard anything more from [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] or [REDACTED] although I did call to confirm that my debt was erased. But now, I went to purchase a home and, like many Americans, find that BrandSource, which is the BNPL third party payment merchant, says I owe the full amount for the fridge. BrandSource is owned by Citi. Before taking up the matter with the credit reporting bureaus, I went to BrandSource and explained why I do not owe the charge and frankly, am surprised I even still have an account with them at all. BrandSource and Citi would not let me forward them the email trail where I have in writing that my debt was forgiven by [REDACTED] [REDACTED]. Instead of a low-cost email paper trail, they want me to print or fax my emails. Fax? I dont have a printer either. BrandSource also said the dispute could take 6-9 months to resolve by Citi, all the while it is on my credit report and could mean hundreds or thousands of more over the life of a home loan. I kept pressing over the course of many frustrating phone calls ( and you can not call Citis resolution department or BrandSources consumer payment department directly, let alone try to communicate with both parts of the company at the same time ). Finally, BrandSource ( Citi ) told me that they can not resolve the dispute at all because they do not have the records from [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] and that they consider my case closed. So, me, a consumer, is stuck trying to resolve a business-to-business records problem involving [REDACTED]. [REDACTED], [REDACTED] [REDACTED], BrandSource, and Citi. I am not empowered to resolve the problems in their business-to-business relationships and the peons they employ at customer service are not really empowered either. But Im still getting an {$1800.00} bill for a fridge which I do not have as well as a further unknown but potentially more costly hit on my credit reportId also like to buy a car My experience demonstrates the danger of getting that credit from a BNPL relationship because there is no central point of responsibility to the consumer if the goods are never delivered as promised. Sub-product: Personal line of credit. Company response to consumer: Closed with explanation. Company public response: Company has responded to the consumer and the CFPB and chooses not to provide a public response. Consumer state: LA. Date received by CFPB: 2022-03-18.

title: Affirm — Credit card: Problem with a purchase shown on your statement
text: On [DATE]/2025, I cancelled an online order with [REDACTED] that was financed through Affirm. This was a cancelled transaction, not a return. No goods were shipped or received. [REDACTED] confirmed the cancellation and confirmed that the funds were returned. Despite this, Affirm failed to promptly cancel the pending loan authorization and continued to hold the transaction in a pending state well beyond its own stated processing cutoff. This restricted access to my funds and created a financial burden for a transaction that never completed. After multiple attempts to resolve the issue directly with Affirm, no corrective action was taken. As a result, I was forced to file a chargeback through my issuing bank, [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] ), solely to protect myself from an indefinite and unjustified funds hold. Only after the chargeback was filed did Affirm void the loan and confirm in writing that the loan was fully cancelled and that I was no longer responsible for it. However, despite this confirmation, [REDACTED] [REDACTED] dispute system continued to freeze the funds under rigid chargeback timelines, treating a cancelled transaction the same as a return. Both Affirm and [REDACTED] [REDACTED] shifted responsibility between each other while the financial burden remained on me as the consumer. This situation demonstrates a systemic failure in which : Cancelled transactions are improperly treated as returns BNPL providers fail to timely release pending authorizations Consumers are forced into chargeback processes to resolve internal processing failures Financial institutions rely on outdated or rigid systems that cause avoidable consumer harm These are not new systems. Both companies operate mature financial infrastructures and should reasonably prevent prolonged consumer harm for cancelled transactions where no goods were delivered and no valid charge finalized. I believe the actions of both Affirm and [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] constitute unfair and deceptive practices, as the financial burden of institutional failures was placed entirely on the consumer. I am requesting CFPB review and corrective action to prevent cancelled BNPL transactions from resulting in prolonged authorization holds and dispute freezes that cause unnecessary financial harm.
